title: Linking Artificial Intelligence Principles
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Workshop on Artificial Intelligence Safety (AAAI-Safe AI 2019)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to compare, organize, and semantically connect a wide range of published Artificial Intelligence (AI) principles. The authors argue that existing AI principles are fragmented, emphasize different values, and cannot individually serve as complete governance frameworks. Their goal is to make common topics and differences across principles explicit so they can be linked and analyzed together.

The paper introduces LAIP (Linking Artificial Intelligence Principles), a platform and methodology for extracting and semantically linking AI principle texts. The authors collected 27 AI principle proposals from academia, nonprofits, government, and industry, then manually identified 10 general topics and expanded keywords using word2vec semantic similarity to improve coverage. They used these topic and keyword groupings to calculate topic coverage and keyword coverage across principle documents, and represented the linkages using RDF/OWL on the LAIP platform.

The work is not an empirical study of AI tools in classrooms or learning settings; it is a framework and document-analysis paper focused on AI governance. The authors conclude that different organizations emphasize different considerations, that semantic expansion improves analysis of principle coverage, and that future AI governance should integrate multiple principle sets into a more comprehensive framework. They also suggest strengthening safety-related considerations, planning for AGI/ASI, and moving from purely human-centered principles toward more harmonious designs that consider both humans and future AI systems.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/text-analysis paper about AI principles and their semantic linking, not an empirical study of educational interventions or student outcomes. It does not evaluate K-12 instruction, AI tutoring, or scientific reasoning outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct measurable impact on K-12 scientific reasoning or inquiry instruction; its contribution is to AI governance and policy taxonomy rather than educational effectiveness.
